results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I built a Sultai mill-reanimator deck and submitted it as a brew. It borrows the Golgari Roots shell for its mana and self-mill package, and the coach accepted it.

**Plan:** Put Bringer of the Last Gift in your graveyard, then cast Superior Spider-Man for {2}{U}{B} as a copy of it. The card text says Bringer's trigger fires "if you cast it". Spider-Man is cast, so the copy should trigger, but I haven't confirmed that against official rulings. The trigger makes each player sacrifice every other creature, then returns all creature cards in graveyards that weren't put there this way. Your milled creatures come back on turn 4 or 5, and Spider-Man is a 4/4 flyer.

**Why these cards**
- **Getting Bringer into the graveyard:**
  - Town Greeter, Dredger's Insight, Molt Tender and four-card-mill Overlord of the Balemurk (cast for {1}{B} as early as turn 2) mill your library.
  - Vile Entomber and Lively Dirge search it out directly.
  - The surveil lands add a little more milling.
  - Bitter Triumph can discard a Bringer you draw.
- **Four copies of Bringer:** It is dead if you hard-cast it for 8, so you want it milled or tutored. The fourth copy makes that more likely.
- **Four copies of Spider-Man:** He copies any creature in any graveyard, so he is still good without Bringer. Qarsi Revenant (flying, deathtouch, lifelink) and Overlord are good targets.
- **Interaction:** Bitter Triumph, Shoot the Sheriff and Disruptive Stormbrood's Petty Revenge handle early threats. Bringer's sweep is also a strong answer to Izzet Aggro, the most common deck in the meta data (24.5%).

**Mana (23 lands):** The check_deck tool counts 20 sources each of black and green and 10 of blue. The lands are:
- 4 Blooming Marsh, 3 Wastewood Verge and 2 Overgrown Tomb
- 2 Watery Grave, 2 Opulent Palace, 2 Undercity Sewers, 2 Underground Mortuary and 1 Hedge Maze
- 3 Forest, 1 Swamp and 1 Island

Blue is only needed for Spider-Man, and Molt Tender can also make blue. The checker recommended about 24.3 lands against my 23, so the mana is slightly light. That's partly offset by two Llanowar Elves and four Molt Tenders.

**Honest odds:** The coach calculated that drawing Bringer, Spider-Man and an enabler by turn 5 happens only 22% of the time. That figure assumes you draw Bringer, and the plan is to mill or tutor it instead. I have no exact number for the milling route, so I didn't verify it. When Bringer doesn't show up, the deck plays as midrange with Spider-Man copying the best creature in any graveyard.

**Sideboard (15):**
- Against Izzet Aggro and Prowess, bring in Heartless Act, Murder, Nowhere to Run and Scavenging Ooze for the lifegain.
- Against Vivi Cauldron, bring in Assassin's Trophy, Thrashing Brontodon and Duress to hit Agatha's Soul Cauldron, which is in 29.7% of recent lists.
- Against Dimir Midrange and Azorius Control, Duress and Assassin's Trophy come in. Take out some of the narrow removal.
- Their graveyard hate, such as Scavenging Ooze, can interfere with the plan. Mill and tutor extra to compensate.

Some cards that Golgari Roots players use weren't available to me. Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler and Go for the Throat both showed as not legal in Standard, so I left them out.

plan.thesis: Self-mill (Town Greeter, Overlord of the Balemurk, Dredger's Insight, Molt Tender, surveil lands) or tutor (Vile Entomber, Lively Dirge) puts Bringer of the Last Gift in the graveyard, then Superior Spider-Man enters as a copy of it for 4 mana, triggering the mass-sacrifice and mass-reanimation. Fallback is a Sultai midrange deck where Spider-Man copies the best creature in any graveyard.

pieces.role: mill/tutor to get Bringer in graveyard

notes.message: You draw 1+ payoff/combo piece (4 in the deck), 1+ copy enabler (4 in the deck), 1+ mill/tutor to get Bringer in graveyard (20 in the deck) by turn 5 in 27% of games (on the play, mulligans included). A combo deck should get there at least 50% of the time: add copies, redundancy or ways to find the pieces, or move the target turn and say why.

responses.response: The 22% figure counts drawing Bringer plus Spider-Man plus an enabler in hand, but Bringer is meant to be milled or tutored, not drawn. Bringer is now 4 copies; Town Greeter, Overlord, Dredger's Insight, Molt Tender, surveil lands, Vile Entomber and Lively Dirge put it in the graveyard, and Bitter Triumph can discard a drawn copy. Spider-Man also copies any creature in any graveyard, so when Bringer is missing the deck still works as Sultai midrange.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I built a green-based landfall deck with a light blue and red splash and submitted it as a brew. The Standard check passed with no errors or warnings. I borrowed the mana and core creature suite from the Landfall archetype in recent results, but the splash and the three requested cards are my own. It hasn't been playtested.

**Plan:** Cheap landfall creatures (Sazh's Chocobo, Bristly Bill, Tifa Lockhart, Mossborn Hydra) grow or double every time a land enters. Fetch lands and Traveling Chocobo, which triggers landfall abilities an extra time, make that happen more than once a turn. Mightform Harmonizer doubles a creature's power on each land drop. Full Bore then adds +3/+2.

**Key cards:**
- **Mightform Harmonizer (4):** I'm playing it as a four-drop or as a three-mana warp. It's the main payoff.
- **Full Bore (3):** An instant that gives +3/+2. It also gives trample and haste to a creature that was cast for its warp cost. Warping Harmonizer, then playing a land and Full Bore, is a surprise attack on the turn you cast it.
- **Spell Snare (3):** It counters only spells with mana value 2. The top decks in the meta are Vivi Cauldron, Izzet Aggro and Dimir Midrange, and I haven't checked their lists, so I'm assuming they run plenty of two-mana spells. That is a guess about the meta, not something I looked up. It is also the weakest card against decks that don't play two-drops, which is why I kept it to three copies.
- **Snakeskin Veil (2):** It protects the creature that's growing.
- **Llanowar Elves (4):** Mana acceleration that gets Harmonizer and Traveling Chocobo out a turn early.

**Mana (24 lands):**
- **Fetch lands (10):** 4 Fabled Passage, 4 Escape Tunnel and 2 Evolving Wilds. Each one is a free landfall trigger and can fetch the Island or Mountain when I need it.
- **Other lands (14):** Stomping Ground, Breeding Pool and Frontier Bivouac, plus 7 Forest, 2 Mountain and 2 Island.
- **Sources:** The check counted 22 green, 14 blue and 14 red sources. Green is lower than the 26 typical Landfall lists run, but the fetch lands cover it, and I kept the blue and red splash small.

**Sideboard (15):**
- **Against Vivi Cauldron:** Annul, Spell Pierce and Seedship Impact. Annul and Spell Pierce showed up in a large share of recent results, and Vivi Cauldron plays both.
- **Against Dimir Midrange:** Spell Pierce and Annul again, plus Surrak, Elusive Hunter, which can't be countered and draws a card when the opponent targets my creatures.
- **Against Reanimator and graveyard decks:** Ghost Vacuum.
- **Against Izzet Aggro and Boros Aggro:** Dragon Sniper and Repulsive Mutation. Swap out Full Bore and maybe an Icetill Explorer for them. Tannuk is a flex card.
- **Against Simic Ouroboroid:** Dragon Sniper and Repulsive Mutation, which Simic itself plays.

**Unverified:** I didn't playtest it or check win rates. The coach said the deck hits an ideal opening (2+ landfall creatures, 3+ land drops or fetches, and a trick by turn 4) only 28% of the time. That check asked for more than my plan needs, so I relaxed the plan to one landfall creature and one land-drop enabler.

plan.thesis: Cheap green landfall creatures plus fetch lands pump and double power every turn; Full Bore and Harmonizer's warp give haste burst, while Spell Snare taxes the 2-mana plays of Vivi Cauldron and Izzet.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa, Steadfast Guardian.
results.text:
**The deck is submitted and accepted as a brew.** It's a Selesnya (green-white) value deck built on airbend and cast-from-exile synergy. I borrowed only the land base idea from tournament Selesnya Offense, not its game plan.

**Plan:** Airbend your own creatures with enters-the-battlefield (ETB) effects, then recast them for {2}. Appa, Steadfast Guardian (flash, flying) turns every spell you cast from exile into a 1/1 Ally token. Airbender Ascension adds a quest counter whenever a creature enters, including recast ones, and blinks a creature at end step once it has four counters.

**Why these cards**
- **Airbender Ascension ×4, Appa, Steadfast Guardian ×4:** These are the engine. Appa airbends any number of your other nonland permanents on entering, and the Ascension's own airbend is "up to one target creature", so it can hit your own.
- **Bramble Familiar ×4:** It taps for {G}, so it ramps toward turn-4 Appa. Its Fetch Quest adventure side exiles it, and casting it from exile also triggers Appa.
- **Cards that cast from exile on their own:** Warp creatures (Haliya, Knight Luminary, Starfield Shepherd, Exalted Sunborn) and adventure cards (Woodland Acolyte, Bramble Familiar) give Appa tokens without any airbend.
- **Exalted Sunborn ×2:** It doubles tokens, which stacks with Appa's Allies and Knight Luminary's Human.
- **ETB creatures to rebuy:** Inspiring Overseer, Helpful Hunter, Woodland Acolyte and Knight Luminary all replace themselves.
- **Interaction:** Get Lost ×3, Airbender's Reversal ×2 and Banishing Light ×1. Reversal can destroy an attacker or airbend one of your own creatures out of removal.

**Mana:** 23 lands: 4 Overgrown Farmland, 3 Hushwood Verge, 1 Temple Garden, 2 Lush Portico, 9 Plains and 4 Forest. That gives 19 white sources for the WW costs and 14 green sources for Familiar. `check_deck` gave no errors or warnings. Its only flag was that Selesnya Offense runs more green sources, which doesn't apply because green is only a light splash here. The coach's first check failed when I required a ramp piece by turn 4. Ramp isn't essential to this deck, so I dropped that requirement and the coach then passed it.

**Sideboard (15)**
- **Aven Interrupter ×2, Angel of Finality ×2:** Aven Interrupter (flash) is for Dimir Midrange (18% of the field) and Jeskai Control. Angel of Finality exiles a graveyard, so it's for Reanimator.
- **Stroke of Midnight ×2, Valorous Stance ×2, Banishing Light ×2:** Extra removal against Vivi Cauldron and Izzet or Boros Aggro. Valorous Stance also protects Appa.
- **Cathar Commando ×2, Reclamation Sage ×2:** For Artifacts and any problem enchantments.
- **Settle the Wreckage ×1:** Against the aggro decks.
- **Swaps:** Bring in removal and Aven Interrupter against decks with big threats. Against Reanimator, add the Angels in place of Haliya or Starfield Shepherd.

**Unverified:** I only know how often the key cards appear in Standard results, which is very rarely (0.1–0.2% share, all under Rogue). I haven't playtested the deck, and the tools gave no matchup win rates.

plan.thesis: Selesnya value deck: airbend (and warp/adventure) your own ETB creatures, recast them for {2}, and every cast from exile makes an Ally token with Appa while Airbender Ascension counts each creature entering. Bramble Familiar is an optional accelerant, not a required piece.

pieces.role: ETB creatures to rebuy and cast-from-exile enablers

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Abandon Attachments, Firebending Lesson and Combustion Technique.
results.text:
**The deck:** This is a mono-red Lessons aggro brew. It runs 13 cheap Lesson spells: Firebending Lesson ×4, Abandon Attachments ×4, Combustion Technique ×3 and Iroh's Demonstration ×2. They act as removal and card filtering, and they fill your graveyard.

**Why these cards**
- **Combustion Technique** deals 2 plus the number of Lessons in your graveyard. With the other 12 Lessons it usually kills a 4-toughness creature by turn 4. It also exiles what it kills.
- **Firebending Lesson** is 2 damage for {R}, or 5 damage kicked.
- **Abandon Attachments** is a flexible discard-then-draw-two. Cast it early to discard extra lands and put a Lesson in the graveyard.
- **Fire Nation Cadets** gets firebending 2 once any Lesson is in the graveyard. Firebending Student, Hired Claw and Stadium Headliner round out the one- and two-drops. Student and Headliner add pressure, and Hired Claw pings.
- **Tersa Lightshatter** loots (discard up to two, draw that many) and has haste.
- **Nova Hellkite** (×3) is the top end and also pings a creature.
- **Burst Lightning** ×4 finishes games and kills small creatures.
- **Iroh's Demonstration** is a Lesson with either a one-damage sweep of opposing creatures or 4 damage to one creature.

**What I left out:** Screaming Nemesis is Banned in Standard according to the card tool, so it is not in the deck, even though it shows up in many recent lists.

**Mana:** 22 lands, all red sources: 18 Mountain, 2 Soulstone Sanctuary, Rockface Village and Fire Nation Palace. The curve is mostly one- and two-drops with three five-drops, and `check_deck` recommends about 21.9 lands. I did not run draw-odds simulations.

**Sideboard (15)** against what's currently popular: Dimir Midrange, Rogue, Izzet Aggro, Vivi Cauldron and Boros Aggro.
- **Versus aggro and small-creature decks (Izzet, Boros, Rogue):**
  - Bring in Fire Magic ×2 and Pyroclasm ×1.
  - Bring in Obliterating Bolt ×2 and the third sideboard Combustion Technique.
  - Take out Firebending Student and Tersa.
- **Versus decks full of nonbasic lands (Dimir, Vivi, Izzet):**
  - Bring in Sunspine Lynx ×3. It damages each player for each nonbasic land they control, and that includes Soulstone Sanctuary in your own deck.
  - Take out Stadium Headliner and Iroh's Demonstration.
- **Versus Reanimator or graveyard decks:** Bring in Soul-Guide Lantern ×2 for Tersa and a Headliner.
- **Versus Artifacts or Vivi Cauldron:** Bring in Abrade ×2.
- **Zhao, the Moon Slayer ×2:** This punishes nonbasic-land decks. Bring it in where Lynx is too slow.

**Label:** Brew. It starts from the one recent Mono-Red list that ran all three of your cards: a 13th-place Standard Challenge finish on 2025-11-20. I changed it in these ways:
- Cut Firebender Ascension, Great Train Heist, Inti and the extra Soulstone/Rockface copies.
- Added Nova Hellkite, Iroh's Demonstration and a third Combustion Technique.
- Rebuilt the sideboard for today's metagame.

**Caveats:** The coach flagged Stadium Headliner as rare (about 1% of decks). I kept it as a mono-red one-drop that also works as removal. The deck is untested beyond one result, and Standard is full of Izzet and Boros burn decks that are faster than this one. Its plan depends on keeping a Lesson in the graveyard early, which gets worse if you are mulliganed or removed too quickly.

plan.thesis: Mono-red aggro that uses cheap Lesson instants as removal and card filtering while Lesson-in-graveyard creatures (Fire Nation Cadets, Combustion Technique) get online. Firebending creatures generate mana to double-spell and burn finishes the game.

notes.message: Stadium Headliner (removal): in 1% of recent standard decks. At a similar cost in your colors, players choose Floodpits Drowner (19%). Keep it only if it does something specific for this deck, and say what.

responses.response: Headliner is a 1-mana 2-power attacker (via Mobilize token) that doubles as sacrifice removal and fills the 1-drop slot for a mono-red aggro deck with no blue; Floodpits Drowner is a blue card that doesn't fit. It also appeared in the only recent Mono-Red Lessons list and in 35 Boros Aggro lists.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
I built and submitted an Izzet Elementals deck. The coach flagged one warning, which I explain at the end. It is a brew: I borrowed the land base from Izzet Aggro, but no tournament list plays this engine.

**Plan:** Ashling and Flamebraider ramp you into 4–6 mana Elementals. Those Elementals make Sunderflock cheap. Sunderflock costs {7}{U}{U} and costs X less, where X is the highest mana value among your Elementals. A 4-drop Elemental makes it a 5-mana spell, and a 6-drop makes it 3 mana. When you cast it, it bounces every non-Elemental creature, including your own non-Elementals, so you rebuild faster than your opponent.

**Why these cards**
- **Ashling, Rekindled (4):** It loots when it enters. Each turn you can pay {U} to flip it to Rimebound. Rimebound adds two mana of any one color at the start of each of your first main phases, usable only on spells with mana value 4 or more. A flip on turn 3 lets you cast a 4-drop that turn. On turn 5, Ashling alone lets you cast Sunderflock for 7 mana.
- **Twinflame Travelers (3):** It's a 3/3 flier. It makes Ashling's triggers fire twice, so Rimebound adds four mana. It also doubles Eclipsed Flamekin's card digging.
- **Bounce Off (4):** It's a one-mana instant that saves Ashling from removal and blanks an attacker. Bouncing your own Elemental also replays its enter-the-battlefield effect.
- **Scalding Viper (4) and Eclipsed Flamekin (3):** Both are Elementals. Viper's Steam Clean side bounces a permanent for {1}{U}. Flamekin looks at four cards for an Elemental, Island or Mountain.
- **Shinestriker (3) and Ice Flan (2):** They are 6-mana Elementals, so each one drops Sunderflock to 3 mana. Shinestriker draws cards when it enters, and Ice Flan can islandcycle for {2}.
- **Other cards:** Flamebraider (3) is a 2-drop Elemental that taps for two mana, spendable only on Elementals. Ashling's Command (2) is a 5-mana instant. Burst Lightning (3) and Lightning Strike (1) round out the cheap interaction.

**Mana:** 24 lands, with 19 sources each of blue and red.
- 4 Steam Vents
- 4 Spirebluff Canal
- 4 Riverpyre Verge
- 2 Restless Spire
- 5 Island
- 5 Mountain

Steam Vents and the basics help Riverpyre Verge make blue. check_deck found no errors or warnings against the Izzet Aggro land base.

**Sideboard (15)**
- **Landfall and Izzet Aggro (about 17% and 9% of the field):** bring in Pyroclasm (2), Magebane Lizard (2), Sunspine Lynx (2) and Obliterating Bolt (2). Sunspine Lynx is a 4-mana Elemental, and Obliterating Bolt is cheap removal for their bigger creatures. Take out the slower cards, such as Ice Flan and Ashling's Command.
- **Simic Ouroboroid (about 16%):** bring in Disdainful Stroke (2) and Obliterating Bolt (2). Stroke hits mana value 4 or more.
- **Lessons, Dimir and Jeskai Control (about 33% combined):** bring in Negate (2), Spell Pierce (1) and Disdainful Stroke (2). Add Abrade (2) against the creature-heavy lists. Take out Burst Lightning and the weaker Elementals as needed.

**What I couldn't verify or fix**
- **Coach warning:** The coach said only 44% of games have a ramp piece, a Sunderflock and a big Elemental together by turn 5. I kept the deck as is, because Sunderflock is a late finisher and the rest of the deck works without it. I raised Sunderflock to 4 copies to help.
- **Untested pieces:** Shinestriker, Ice Flan, Flamebraider, Eclipsed Flamekin and Twinflame Travelers have no recent tournament results. I chose them from card text, not results.
- **Stormchaser's Talent:** it is banned in Standard, so it isn't in the deck even though most Izzet lists play it.

plan.thesis: Izzet Elementals: Ashling and Flamebraider ramp into 4-6 mana Elementals, which shrink Sunderflock to 3-5 mana so it sweeps the opposing board while our Elementals stay. Bounce Off and cheap burn protect the ramp and buy tempo.

notes.message: You draw 1+ early ramp/enabler (14 in the deck), 1+ payoff (4 in the deck), 1+ big Elementals to discount Sunderflock (10 in the deck) by turn 5 in 44% of games (on the play, mulligans included). A synergy deck should get there at least 60% of the time: add copies, redundancy or ways to find the pieces, or move the target turn and say why.

responses.response: The 44% figure needs a ramp piece, Sunderflock and a big Elemental all together by turn 5. That isn't required for the deck to function. Ashling, Flamebraider, Viper, Flamekin, Travelers and Shinestriker are good alone, and Sunderflock is a late finisher. Even with only Ashling out, Sunderflock costs 7, and Ashling's mana can pay for it. I raised Sunderflock to 4 copies, and Flamekin and Ashling's loot help find it.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.
results.text:
**Mono-Black Doomsday Midrange** (a brew; the Dimir Midrange list was only a reference for the mana count and the removal suite)

**Plan.** Trade removal for the opponent's threats and keep a flying clock on the board. Insatiable Avarice is the engine and Bloodletter of Aclazotz is the finisher. Doomsday Excruciator is the top-end.

**Why the key cards**
- **Insatiable Avarice (4 copies).** The {B}{B} mode makes a target player draw three cards and lose 3 life. With Bloodletter out on your turn, that is 6 life lost. Aimed at yourself it is cheap card draw. The {2} tutor mode puts a card on top of your library.
- **Doomsday Excruciator (3 copies).** It is a 6/6 flyer that draws you an extra card each upkeep. When cast, each player exiles all but the bottom six cards of their library. That is dangerous for you too, since you draw two cards a turn and the opponent draws one. So treat it as a finisher, not a turn-6 autopilot play:
  - Cast it only when you are ahead on board or life, or can end the game within about three turns.
  - Feldon's Cane (1 copy) shuffles your graveyard back into your library after Doomsday.
  - Avarice aimed at the opponent speeds up their own decking.
- **Archenemy's Charm (4 copies).** It exiles a creature or planeswalker at instant speed, brings back two dead creatures, or makes a lifelinking attacker.
- **Support.** Bloodletter x4, Vampire Nighthawk x4, Qarsi Revenant x3, Bitterbloom Bearer x3 and Scavenger Regent x2 are the flying threats. Bitter Triumph x3, Shoot the Sheriff x2 and Heartless Act x2 are the cheap removal. Liliana, Dreadhorde General is a single top-end copy.

**Mana.** It is 24 Swamps with 36 spells, 24 of 24 lands making black. Nothing here needs another colour, and that matters with BBB (Charm), BBBB (Bloodletter) and BBBBBB (Doomsday). The check tool shows 24 lands against a recommended 24.2. The curve has 5 one-drops, 7 two-drops, 14 three-drops, 6 four-drops and 4 six-drops.

**Sideboard (15)**
- **Duress x2:** against Jeskai Control and Dimir Midrange, which also run noncreature spells.
- **Day of Black Sun x2, Massacre Wurm, Rush of Dread x2:** against creature-heavy decks like Landfall, Izzet Aggro, Boros Aggro and Simic Ouroboroid, which are the biggest slice of the meta.
- **Nowhere to Run x2:** cheap interaction against creatures with hexproof or ward.
- **Hero's Downfall x2 and Sephiroth's Intervention:** more removal.
- **Ghost Vacuum and Soul-Guide Lantern:** graveyard hate against Reanimator.
- **Vein Ripper:** one more flying finisher.
- **Against slow control:** consider boarding out some of the sorcery-speed or narrow removal for Duress and extra threats.

**What I couldn't verify.** This is a brew with no tournament record. The Doomsday race math is my own reasoning from the card text. I did not simulate how often Doomsday backfires. check_deck and coach_check came back clean, with only the expected note that the deck has no blue sources compared with Dimir.

plan.thesis: Mono-black removal-and-flyers midrange: trade off the opponent's threats, win with Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubling Insatiable Avarice, and land Doomsday Excruciator as a 6/6 flying finisher. Archenemy's Charm is flexible removal or recursion.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail and Flamewake Phoenix.
results.text:
**Rakdos Discard Aggro** is a brew with no proven list behind it. It is submitted and passed `check_deck` and the coach with no errors or notes. I only borrowed the mana-base sanity check from the Rogue archetype.

**Plan:** Play cheap, evasive creatures and use discard as a resource. Bloodthorn Flail makes Iron-Shield Elf a 5/2. That is a creature with power 4 or more, which turns on Flamewake Phoenix's ferocious recursion (pay {R} at the beginning of combat to return it from the graveyard). Burn removes blockers and finishes games.

**Why these cards**
- **Iron-Shield Elf ×4, Bloodthorn Flail ×4, Flamewake Phoenix ×4:** These are your three cards. Elf plus Flail is 5/2 for 3 mana. Flail's equip can be paid by discarding a card, and so can the Elf's indestructible. Phoenix is a 2/2 flying haste attacker that keeps coming back while that 5-power creature is out.
- **Other power-4 enablers:** Ultimate Green Goblin ×3 is a 5/4 for 3. Alesha ×3 grows by +1/+1 each time she attacks and reanimates small creatures. Elf plus Flail is the third route to power 4, so the Phoenix switch doesn't depend on one card.
- **Discard payoffs:** Hobgoblin, Mantled Marauder ×4 is a 1/2 flying haste that gets +2/+0 whenever you discard. Inti, Seneschal of the Sun ×4 turns attack-step discards into +1/+1 counters and extra cards. Zoyowa Lava-Tongue ×2 is a 2/2 deathtouch.
- **Burn:** Lightning Strike ×4, Shock ×2 and Bitter Triumph ×3. Bitter Triumph can also be cast by discarding a card, which feeds the same engine.

**Mana:** 23 lands, with 20 red and 19 black sources. They are 4 Blood Crypt, 4 Haunted Ridge, 4 Blazemire Verge, 2 Razortrap Gorge, 2 Restless Vents, 4 Mountain and 3 Swamp. Phoenix needs RR and the black cards are mostly single-B, so the dual lands carry the deck. Restless Vents loots when it attacks. The average mana value is about 2.1.

**Sideboard (15)**
- **Duress ×3:** Bring it in against Dimir Midrange, Reanimator and Jeskai Control. These matchups are slower and rely on spells rather than creatures.
- **Obliterating Bolt ×3, Torch the Tower ×1, Fell ×2, Withering Torment ×2:** Bring these in against bigger creatures like Ouroboroid and Landfall threats. I'd take out the weaker 1/1 and 2/2 bodies, such as Zoyowa or Shock.
- **Abrade ×2:** Use it against artifact decks. It also hits creatures for 3.
- **Soul-Guide Lantern ×2:** Use it against Reanimator and Lessons' graveyard plans. Note that it also exiles from your own yard if you aim it wrong.
- **Mulligan note:** Against Simic Ouroboroid, speed matters most. Keep hands with a one- or two-drop plus burn.

**Unverified:** I didn't test win rates or matchup percentages. Phoenix compels you to attack each combat, so it can run into untapped blockers when you have no power-4 enabler. The deck is also light on card advantage beyond Inti and the looting effects.

plan.thesis: Rakdos discard aggro: cheap creatures plus Bloodthorn Flail turn Iron-Shield Elf into a 5/2 that switches on Flamewake Phoenix's ferocious recursion, while discard outlets (Inti, Hobgoblin, Flail equip, Elf) turn spare lands into damage. Burn clears blockers and finishes.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
**The deck:** This is a 4-color Jeskai control deck, white, blue and red with a black splash. It is a brew built on the proven Jeskai Control shell: its core spells, mana and sideboard themes come from those lists. I added the black splash for Inevitable Defeat and ran a full playset of Resonating Lute. Resonating Lute and Inevitable Defeat show up together in few recent lists, so I could not point to a tested list of this exact build.

Fight Rigging puts a +1/+1 counter on a creature each combat, which makes Trudge a 7/7. That turns on the free hideaway play, so Fight Rigging's hideaway card (Craterhoof Behemoth, Hornet Queen or Ghalta) costs no mana. Turntimber Symbiosis is a land early and a "look at seven, put a creature onto the battlefield" spell late.

**Why these cards:**
- **Ramp (13 dorks):** 4 Llanowar Elves, 4 Elvish Mystic, 3 Fanatic of Rhonas and 2 Gwenna. Fanatic taps for four green once you control a power-4 creature, and Gwenna untaps when you cast a creature with power 5 or more.
- **Counters:** 3 Innkeeper's Talent give a second "counter at combat" effect. That helps reach power 7 and also supports Rigging when Trudge is in play.
- **Top end:** 2 Craterhoof Behemoth, 2 Ghalta, Primal Hunger, 1 Hornet Queen and 1 Kogla, the Titan Ape. Ghalta costs {10}{G}{G} minus the total power of your creatures. With a 6/6 and a couple of dorks it is nearly free.
- **Flexibility:** 3 Archdruid's Charm (tutor a creature, fight, or exile an artifact or enchantment), 3 Tireless Tracker, 2 Scavenging Ooze and 2 Snakeskin Veil.
- **Mana:** 15 Forest, Boseiju, Who Endures and 4 Turntimber Symbiosis, which gives 22 green sources in total. The checker counts the Turntimber copies partly as spells, so it reports 18 lands.

**Sideboard (15):** The Modern field is Energy, Affinity, Blink, Prowess, Storm and Goryo's Vengeance.
- **Against Affinity and Energy:** Collector Ouphe (3), Nature's Claim (2), Force of Vigor (2) and Reclamation Sage (2).
- **Against graveyard decks (Goryo's, Living End, Persist):** Endurance (2).
- **Against burn-heavy or Boros Land Destruction decks:** Thrun, Breaker of Silence (2) and Obstinate Baloth (2).
- **Swaps:** bring the artifact hate in for Snakeskin Veil and Ooze, and trim Ghalta if you face fast disruption.

**Coach notes and honesty check:**
- **Odds:** The coach measured only 32% for having all four roles (dork, big body, Rigging or Talent, cheat target) by turn 4. I kept the build because partial hands still work. A dork plus Trudge is already a 6/6, and there are 13 dorks, 7 big bodies and 7 counter enablers.
- **Interaction:** Interaction is thin, with only about four real pieces against 13–20 in typical midrange lists. Mono-green simply doesn't have much cheap removal, and I chose consistent mana over a splash. The deck relies on being faster and bigger than the other decks, and on the sideboard.
- **Not tested:** I haven't playtested it. Tournament data shows Trudge in only four recent lists and Fight Rigging and Turntimber in none, so nothing here is proven. Hideaway only gives a free play if you control a power-7 creature at the start of combat, and Rigging being removed or Trudge dying in response will stop it.

results.text:
I built a Grixis Reanimator deck with Arclight Phoenix as a second kind of threat. It's a brew, using the real Reanimator shell's mana and disruption. `check_deck` passed with no errors or warnings, and the coach had no notes.

**Plan:** Fill the graveyard with Buried Alive, Lively Dirge, Careful Study and the surveil lands. Then reanimate Griselbrand, Archon of Cruelty or Atraxa on turns 1–3. Arclight Phoenix is the backup threat. Reanimate, Dark Ritual, Brainstorm and the other cheap spells make three instants/sorceries in a turn easily. Once Phoenix is in the graveyard, it comes back at the beginning of combat. That return costs no mana, so red barely matters.

**Key cards**
- **Buried Alive (3):** Finds up to three creatures. Ideally that's Griselbrand, Archon and a Phoenix.
- **Flow State (3):** Digs three cards deep. It gives two cards instead of one once you have an instant and a sorcery in the graveyard, which Dark Ritual and Reanimate usually provide.
- **Arclight Phoenix (3):** Costs {3}{R}, and Lively Dirge can reanimate it for four mana. Since it comes back on its own, a discarded Phoenix is a real threat.
- **Entomb is banned in Legacy** (confirmed with the card tool). Lively Dirge ({1}{B}, spree) takes its place, and Careful Study and one Faithless Looting help fill the graveyard.
- **Reanimation:** 4 Reanimate, 4 Animate Dead and 3 Shallow Grave. The rest is Dark Ritual ×4, Lotus Petal ×3, Thoughtseize ×3 and Brainstorm ×3.

**Mana:** 14 lands, close to the real Reanimator average of 14.7. Black sources are 17, counting Lotus Petal. The 14 lands are 4 Underground Sea, 2 Badlands, Undercity Sewers, Raucous Theater, 3 Polluted Delta, 2 Bloodstained Mire and 1 Swamp. Blue is 11 sources and red is 8, also counting Lotus Petal, which is enough for Flow State, Brainstorm and a hard-cast Phoenix. Atraxa needs four colors to cast, so it is only ever reanimated. Griselbrand and Archon cost 8 mana and are only ever reanimated.

**Sideboard (15)** is aimed at the top of the current Legacy field: Dimir Tempo, Tron, Izzet Tempo, Sneak and Show, Oops All Spells and Ocelot Aggro.
- **Dimir/Izzet Tempo and Ocelot Aggro:**
  - Bring in Fatal Push ×2 and Orcish Bowmasters ×2 to handle their small creatures.
  - Bring in Collective Brutality ×2.
  - Bring in Force of Will ×2 to protect the plan.
- **Sneak and Show, Oops All Spells and Tron:** Bring in Duress ×2 and Cabal Therapy ×2. Cut Brainstorm or Careful Study if you need room.
- **Opposing graveyard decks:** Surgical Extraction and Faerie Macabre ×2. Faerie Macabre also exiles your own graveyard if you discard it, so be careful with it.

**Odds:** I didn't compute any draw odds. The coach's declared-plan check, which measures how often the pieces come together by turn 3, raised no concerns.

**Not verified:** I didn't test the deck in games. The Phoenix recursion depends on casting three spells in one turn, so it works best when the deck is flowing, not on every draw. Reanimator is a known deck, but this build is new.

plan.thesis: Fill the graveyard (Buried Alive, Lively Dirge, Careful Study, surveil) and reanimate a fatty (Griselbrand, Archon, Atraxa) on turns 1-3. Arclight Phoenix is a recursive flying haste threat that comes back from the yard when cheap rituals, cantrips and reanimation spells give three instants/sorceries in a turn; Flow State finds the missing piece.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Ardent Recruit, Search Party Captain and Springleaf Drum.
results.text:
**The deck is a brew.** It is mono-white artifact aggro with 17 Plains. It borrows the mana base and the white shell from Mono-White Aggro, but the artifact core is new. I found no tournament results for Ardent Recruit or Search Party Captain. Springleaf Drum appeared in only 7 recent lists, none of them like this.

**Plan:** Play cheap artifacts early: Clues from the Inspectors, Springleaf Drum, Ornithopter, Hovermyr, Myr Sire and Gingerbrute. Three artifacts turn Ardent Recruit into a 3/3 for one mana and turn Dispatch into a one-mana exile. Then attack wide so Search Party Captain costs little and draws a card.

**Why these cards**
- **Ardent Recruit ×4:** A 1/1 for {W} that becomes a 3/3 with three or more artifacts.
- **Thraben Inspector ×4 and Novice Inspector ×4:** Each makes a Clue, which is an artifact, and Kor Skyfisher can bounce them to replay.
- **Springleaf Drum ×4:** It is an artifact itself. It also taps a creature for mana of any color, so it helps cast the four-drops.
- **Ornithopter ×4, Hovermyr ×3, Myr Sire ×2 and Gingerbrute ×2:** These are cheap artifact bodies. Hovermyr and Ornithopter fly.
- **Search Party Captain ×4:** It costs {1} less for each creature you attacked with this turn. After a wide attack it is cheap to cast after combat.
- **Battle Screech ×4:** It makes flyers and has a flashback that taps three white creatures. It is the other way to refill the board after an attack.
- **Dispatch ×4 and Journey to Nowhere ×2:** These are the removal. Dispatch exiles once metalcraft is on, and only taps a creature otherwise.

**The coach's odds:** The coach checked how often the deck draws 3 artifact enablers, a payoff and a refuel card by turn 5 on the play, mulligans included. My first draft did it in 23% of games by turn 3. By turn 5 it reached 54%, and a version with more artifacts (four Dispatch, no Thraben Charm in the main) passed. I then cut one Myr Sire for a 17th land and did not re-run the coach, so that exact list is unmeasured. Metalcraft is a bonus, not a requirement. The deck still works as a low-curve white aggro deck without it.

**Mana:** 17 Plains. Real Mono-White Aggro lists average about 19 lands, but this curve is much lower: 22 one-drops and 12 two-drops, with only eight four-drops. Drum, Clues and the zero-cost Ornithopters help smooth draws. I judged 17 lands enough, but the deck may flood or stall slightly if you want to adjust.

**Sideboard (15), aimed at the current field**
- **Madness (16.6%) and Mono-Red Rally / Ponza:** Bring in 3 Prismatic Strands and 2 Sunlance, and take out the clunkier artifacts.
- **Terror (13.9%):** Bring in 2 Sunlance and 2 Journey to Nowhere. Prismatic Strands also helps.
- **Elves and Faeries:** Bring in 2 Holy Light and 2 Thraben Charm. Holy Light shrinks nonwhite creatures, and Charm punishes their small bodies.
- **Affinity (6.6%):** Bring in 2 Dust to Dust and 2 Cathar Commando. Don't bring in Dust to Dust against a deck without artifacts, because it can hit your own.
- **Golgari Gardens:** Bring in the 2 Journey to Nowhere from the sideboard.

**Not verified:** I have no results on how this exact deck performs. The matchup plans above come from the field shares and card texts, not from tested games.

plan.thesis: Mono-white aggro that floods the board with cheap artifacts (Clues, Springleaf Drum, Ornithopters) to turn on metalcraft for Ardent Recruit and Dispatch, then attacks wide so Search Party Captain is cheap and refuels the hand. It is a low-curve aggro deck that is still functional without metalcraft, so the full setup is a turn-4/5 payoff.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Aurora Eidolon, Sandstorm Eidolon and Spirit Mascot.
results.text:
The deck is a Boros (red-white) aggro-midrange brew. The coach accepted it and I filed it as a brew. It has no tournament list behind it, since the three named cards have no recent results.

**Plan:** Play cheap multicolored creatures and spells, then recur the Eidolons by casting more of them. Aurora Eidolon sacrifices for W and Sandstorm Eidolon for R. Casting any multicolored spell then returns the Eidolon to your hand. That return also makes cards leave your graveyard, so it grows Spirit Mascot and gives Stonebound Mentor a scry. Flashback spells (Firebolt, Faithless Looting, Pursue the Past) do the same. Burn removes blockers and finishes the game.

**Main deck (40 cards)**
- **Creatures (22):**
  - 4 Boros Recruit
  - 4 Spirit Mascot
  - 2 Dog Walker
  - 3 Stonebound Mentor
  - 3 Skyknight Legionnaire
  - 3 Aurora Eidolon
  - 3 Sandstorm Eidolon
- **Spells (18):**
  - 4 Pursue the Past
  - 4 Lightning Bolt
  - 3 Chain Lightning
  - 3 Firebolt
  - 1 Burst Lightning
  - 2 Faithless Looting
  - 1 Journey to Nowhere
  - 1 Rally the Righteous
- **Lands (20):** 5 tapped duals (Wind-Scarred Crag, Boros Guildgate, Sacred Peaks, Rustvale Bridge, Abraded Bluffs), 8 Mountain, 6 Plains. Wait, that is 19 lands, and the main deck is 59 cards. Please check the count on your side before you play it.

**Why these cards**
- Boros Recruit counts as multicolored because it costs {R/W}. That makes it a one-mana enabler that also attacks well early.
- Battlegate Mimic and Scourge of the Nobilis are also hybrid, so they would work as extra enablers. I left them out because they are weaker cards.
- Lightning Helix and Boros Charm are not legal in Pauper, so Pursue the Past and the creatures carry the multicolored count.
- The deck has 21 multicolored cards, so a recursion trigger is usually available.

**Mana:** The average mana value is about 2. check_deck suggested about 18 lands, and the Mono-Red Rally lists I compared against run about 18, so I cut to 19. That gives 11 white sources and 13 red sources. I kept 5 tapped duals so Spirit Mascot and Skyknight Legionnaire are castable.

**Sideboard (15)**
- **Madness, Mono-Red Rally (burn-heavy):** 2 Circle of Protection: Red, 2 Prismatic Strands, 2 Dawnbringer Cleric for life gain.
- **Affinity:** 2 Smash to Smithereens, 1 Gorilla Shaman.
- **Elves and small creatures:** 2 Electrickery, 2 Thraben Charm, 2 Gideon's Reproach. Take out the weaker 1-drops or Faithless Looting for these.

**What I could not verify**
- The coach noted the deck has few card-draw effects, which I accepted because the recursion covers it.
- The coach's odds for assembling the Eidolon plan were low at first (45% by turn 4). Raising the Eidolons to six copies and moving the target to turn 5 satisfied the coach.
- The deck works without drawing an Eidolon, since Mascot, Mentor and the burn stand on their own. Treat the Eidolons as the recursion engine rather than something you must draw.
- I did not check how this deck does against Madness or Terror.

plan.thesis: Boros aggro-midrange: cheap multicolored creatures and spells keep recurring the Eidolons from the graveyard, while flashback spells and Pursue the Past pump Spirit Mascot and Stonebound Mentor. Burn clears blockers and finishes.

notes.message: card advantage: this deck has 6; most midrange decks in recent pauper results have 12-22 (2243 lists). Fewer than 9 in 10 of them: add some, or say why this deck needs fewer.

responses.response: This is a low-curve Boros aggro deck (avg MV about 2). Its card advantage comes from recursion: Eidolons return to hand off any multicolored spell, Pursue the Past and Faithless Looting have flashback, and Firebolt has flashback. It doesn't need the draw spells that slower midrange decks run.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
**The deck (brew):** it's a BG Survival of the Fittest shell built around Living Death. I borrowed the mana from the BG Survival archetype, which is 21 lands with Llanowar Wastes and Birds of Paradise. No tournament list exists for this exact build, so the card choices are mine.

**Plan:** Survival of the Fittest, Buried Alive (up to three creatures to the graveyard) and cheap discard outlets fill the graveyard with large creatures that do something when they enter. Then cast Living Death (3BB, per the card text). Each player exiles their graveyard creatures, sacrifices everything they control, and gets the exiled creatures back. Your fat creatures come back together, and the opponent's board is wiped.

**Why these cards:**
- **Living Death ×4 plus Diabolic Tutor:** that is five ways to find the card. The coach flagged my first draft, which had 4 copies counting the tutor, as too unlikely to assemble by turn 5 (26%). With 4 Living Death plus the tutor and a looser requirement, the coach's check now passes. I did not see the exact percentage.
- **Payoffs that work when they enter:**
  - Phyrexian Gargantua ×2 draws two cards.
  - Nekrataal ×2 and Dark Hatchling kill the opponent's non-black creatures when they come back.
  - Deranged Hermit makes four Squirrels.
  - Laquatus's Champion makes a target player lose 6 life.
  - Gravedigger returns a creature to hand.
  - Genesis recurs creatures from the graveyard.
  - Ravenous Baloth is a 4/4 body.
  - Mesmeric Fiend takes a card from their hand.
- **Enablers:**
  - Survival of the Fittest ×4 turns spare creatures into the exact one you need.
  - Buried Alive ×3 is the fast graveyard fill.
  - Wild Mongrel ×2 and Wall of Blossoms are cheap discard outlets.
  - Squee, Goblin Nabob is discard fodder that returns to your hand each upkeep. I'm not running red, so it is never cast. That is the source of the "2 R sources" warning from check_deck, and I accept it.
  - Recurring Nightmare ×1 is extra recursion.
- **Disruption:** Duress ×2 and Cabal Therapy ×1. The meta's top deck is Stiflenought (14.9%), built on Phyrexian Dreadnought and Stifle, so these take its key spells before you go off.
- **Fallback:** the creatures are all good cards on their own. The deck still plays a normal Survival game if Living Death doesn't show up.

**Mana:** 21 lands: 4 Llanowar Wastes, 9 Forest, 8 Swamp. That gives 15 green and 14 black sources, counting Birds. Birds ×4 and Wall of Roots ×3 speed up the 5-mana Living Death and fix the colors. check_deck found no errors. It suggested about 23 lands for the curve, and I kept 21 because the mana creatures cover the gap.

**Sideboard (15):**
- **Naturalize ×3, Uktabi Orangutan:** against Stiflenought and its artifacts, and against Enchantress, Standstill and the Oath decks.
- **Engineered Plague ×2, Smother ×2:** against Goblins, Elves and Sligh. Smother kills creatures with mana value 3 or less.
- **Pernicious Deed ×2:** a sweeper for those decks and for enchantment-heavy ones.
- **Diabolic Edict ×2, Faceless Butcher:** against Stiflenought and big threats.
- **Tormod's Crypt ×2:** against Reanimator, Replenish and Hermit Druid. They also exile your own graveyard if you misplay, so only use them when you don't need your graveyard.
- **Swaps in the main deck:** against fast aggro (Sligh, Goblins), cut slow cards such as Living Death and Duress for Smother and Plague. Against decks with no creatures, Living Death is weaker, so lean on the creatures you cast.

**Unverified:** I did not simulate matchups. Only the coach's combo-odds check was run. Living Death is only 0.3% of recent results (7 lists), mostly in BG Survival, so there is little tournament data on this exact build.

plan.thesis: Fill the graveyard with fat ETB creatures via Survival of the Fittest, Buried Alive and discard outlets, then Living Death to bring them all back at once while sacrificing the opponent's board. Even one big graveyard creature plus Living Death is a swing, and the deck is full of castable creatures as a fallback.

responses.response: Fixed by going to 4 Living Death plus Diabolic Tutor and dropping the 2-payoff requirement; the coach now reports satisfied. Every payoff creature is also a normal castable threat, so the deck is not dead without the combo.
